parole.significato: A pork rib dish cooked in broth, popular in Malaysia and Singapore.
parole.testo: From Malay bak kut teh, from Hokkien 肉骨茶 (bah-kut-tê).

parole.significato: Informal term of address for a male warrant officer in the Singapore Armed Forces.
parole.testo: From Malay encik, from Hokkien 引叔 (ín-chek, “uncle”).

parole.significato: A traditional style of eatery having public seating and multiple vendors selling Chinese, Indian, and Malay food.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Malay kopitiam, from Hokkien 咖啡店 (ko-pi-tiàm), in turn from Malay kopi (“coffee”).

parole.significato: Bite-sized snack or dessert foods in Malaysia and nearby countries, usually made from rice and often brightly coloured.
parole.testo: From Malay kuih, from Hokkien 粿 (kóe, “rice cake”).

parole.significato: A bite-sized buttery, crumbly pastry filled with pineapple jam and served during festivities in Malaysia, Singapore, In…
parole.testo: From kuih + tart, the former word from Malay kuih, from Hokkien 粿 (kóe, “rice cake”).

parole.significato: Placed at the end of a sentence to accentuate the mood or attitude of the speaker.
parole.testo: From Malay lah, Hokkien 啦 (--la) and Cantonese 啦 (laa¹). Doublet of la in colloquial Hong Kong English.
